To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) exceptions can be expressed in a single intermediate language that is independent of the target hardware and operating system, and (2) this intermediate language can support all the major implementation techniques for exceptions.

(a) exceptions can be implemented in a single, uniform, architecture-independent framework; (b) the framework supports four of the best-known exception-handling techniques; (c) the framework can be used to implement exceptions in a variety of architectures; (d) the framework allows the compiler to make the choice of exception-handling policy; and (e) the framework allows a single optimizer that is oblivious to the exception-handling policy to optimize exception-handling code.

(a) a single intermediate language can support multiple exception-handling mechanisms, and (b) a standard optimizer can be used to optimize exception-handling code, provided it is given the appropriate dataflow information.
